#### **<u>Highlights</u>** 

China will cut its 2012 growth target to an eight-year low of 7.5 percent and hold the CPI target at around 4 percent, according to the government work report delivered by Premier Wen Jiabao at the Fifth Session of the Eleventh National People's Congress on March 5, 2012. Facing many difficulties, as slumping housing market and export downturn of domestic autos and household appliances, when will copper consumption season? Representatives have their ideas on copper. 

Li Yihuang, Deputy to the NPC and President of Jiangxi Copper Group Co, thought that copper fundamentals would gave support for copper prices in H1 2012 and copper prices have strong momentum in short term. He estimated that copper consumption would rise by 7% y/y but would fluctuate due to uncertainties around global economy. 

Wei Jianghong, Deputy to the NPC and President of Tongling Nonferrous Metal Group Co Ltd, thought that Chinese c

opper consumption growth would be about 6%, the lowest since 2008. 

Zhou Zhongshu, President of Minmetals, thought that average price of nonferrous metal would decrease by 20% in 2012, but better than ferrous metals. Besides, he supported Chinese enterprises to invest in overseas mines and revealed that Minmetals would continue seeking copper, aluminum, lead, zinc and nickel projects to invest in. 

From the view of copper end-using industries, power industry especially power grid was a bright spot for copper consumption. Xue Yusheng, academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering (CAE) suggested that smart grid should be included into _National Energy Strategy Plan_ and give preferential policies, as fiscal and taxation, electricity price, investment and financing. Etc. polices. 

Markets Awaits Supportive Policy. As financial costs squeeze profits, copper enterprises attach high importance to whether or not the government will introduce some supportive measures for the copper industry. Home appliances enterprises hoped that governments gave higher purchasing subsidies for energy efficiency household appliances, which was controlled at about 5% of total commodity price. 

In Q1, Chinese copper consumption has been in a slump; domestic refined copper net import greatly increased in first two months of 2012, which was higher than actual demand and thus led to huge inventory accumulation; copper prices was expected to have a relatively weak performance in Q2 and Q3 of 2012, due to Chinese domestic destocking process. 

#### **Copper Market Commentary** 

###### **Copper prices fluctuate at a narrow range** 

Copper for three month on LME opened at USD8,515/t on Mar.1, and closed at USD8,445/t on Mar.30, touching a high of USD8,629/t on Mar.1 and a low of USD8,290/t on Mar.6. 

LME copper stock continued to decline, down to 256kt on Mar 30, a slightly rise from the lowest level 

of 254kt on Mar 26. At the same period, cancelled warrants stayed at a high level, which indicated a

further decline for LME copper stock in future. 

After a final agreement on Greek financial assistance, The European Central Bank (ECB) has left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 1%. It is the second time the ECB has offered such three-year loans, coming after 489bn euros were lent out in December. Although Greece temporarily avoided default, how to let economy completely get well is the key of all problems. However there are still many uncertainties. Besides, rising dollar index gave pressures on copper prices, which ever hit 81 at the middle of March. Federal Reserve Chairman Ben S. Bernanke said on March 26 that while he’s encouraged by the decline in the unemployment rate, continued accommodative monetary policy will be needed. The central bank bought $2.3 trillion of debt in two rounds of quantitative easing that ended in June 2011, during which LME 3-Month copper prices increased by 2% against previous tr

ading day. 

Copper for three month delivery on SHFE opened at 60,500 yuan/t on Mar.2, and closed at 61,060 yuan/t on Mar.30, touching a high of 61,180 yuan/t on Mar.2 and a low of 59, 390 yuan/t on Mar.7. 

Domestic copper inventory in SHFE kept rising since entering into March of 2012, still at the high level of over 220kt. Copper stocks in domestic bonded warehouses were estimated to stay at 600-700kt, with the same level of last year. Great stocks showed that domestic copper consumption was still weak, which gave great pressure on copper prices. In the short term, copper inventory in domestic Exchanges and bonded warehouses might rise and worries for Chinese copper consumption will still continue. 

Chinese metal market and the stock market lose upward momentum in early March as the government at the Fifth Session of the 11th National People's Congress (NPC) set the GDP growth target at 7.5% for 2012, down from 8 percent in 2011. This is the first time for the Chinese government to lower its economic growth target after keeping it around 8 percent for seven consecutive years. Besides, China's premier Wen said on Mar. 14 that the country won’t slacken it efforts in regulating the housing prices, which he considered still “far from coming back to a reasonable level” despite curbs imposed to discourage a flurry of speculative buying. Wen called for long-term, steady and sound development of China's property market, saying the gains will be lost and chaos will occur in the housing sector if the current regulations are loosened. Although copper consumption in building and construction accounted for only 8%, Chinese tight policy on real estate market will give pressures on copper prices. 

From a technical point of view, LME copper prices will keep between USD8,300-8,400/t, weak character is obvious, due to lack of clear direction. 30-day moving average has a better support. On the whole, technical indicators are not bearish, but trend not clear. It is estimated that concussion pattern will continue, but lack of absolute unilateral speculative opportunity, with 61,000-62,000 yuan/t as a watershed.

###### **Chinese refined copper production remains at a relative high level** 

According to data from China Nonferrous metals Industry Association (CNIA), domestic refined copper output was 438kt in Feb and accumulated output reached 872kt during Jan to Feb, a rise of 7.3% y/y. According to data released by National Bureau of Statistics of China (NBS), refined copper output reached 437kt in Feb and accumulated output was 870kt during Jan to Feb, up by 6.9% y/y. Antaike’s statistics showed that output of domestic 12 copper cathode producers reached 326.2kt in Feb, up by 5.64% m/m; and accumulated output of domestic 12 copper cathode producers reached 635kt during Jan to Feb, a rise of 6.69% compared to the same period of last year. Based on above

data, Antaike calculated domestic refined copper output of abou855kt in the first two months, a rise of 7.82% y/y. 

Domestic copper-in-concentrate output during Jan to Feb 2012 was 171kt, up by 15.78% y/y. Jiangxi, Inner Mongolia, Yunnan, Anhui and etc. as Chinese large production regions for copper concentrate produced more than 61% of the total Chinese copper concentrates. 

Domestic copper semis output was 914kt In Feb and accumulated output reached 1.59Mt during Jan to Feb, a rise of 18.8% y/y. Large copper semis producer made great contribution to Chinese copper semis production growth. Facing all kinds of management difficulties and capital shortage, Chinese large copper fabricating enterprises crowded out small companies whose orders were getting less and less. According to Antaike’s survey, operating rate in wire and rod enterprises is relative high, which has benefitted from strong consumption in electricity power industry; operating rate in copper tube is slowly getting better after one week holiday for the Spring Festival in Jan. Although effected by lower operating rate in copper fabricating enterprises, domestic copper semis output still increased due to domestic production capacity expansion, earnings have not been optimistic.

###### **Chinese refined copper imports continue to rise in Feb** 

According to data released by China’s Customs, refined copper import was 376kt in Feb, up by 12.0% m/m; accumulated refined copper import reached 711kt, up by 76.2% y/y. February import of refined copper got more than expected, due to concentrated customs declaration for copper stockpile which entered in Jan, or lagged delivery caused by the Spring Festival Holidays. Refined copper export increased to 700t, 13 times more than 51t in Jan. accumulated export of refined copper during Jan to Feb decreased about 98% against the same period of 2011. Under current situations of domestic refined copper supply surplus and lower LME/SHFE arbitrage, it is unlikely for refined copper export to sharply rise as that in H1 2011. 

Copper scrap import reached 400kt in Feb, higher than 230kt in Jan. It has been not cost-effective for copper scraps to be used as raw materials since the second half of 2011 and copper scrap import has been influence to a certain extent. It will be unfavorable for importing copper scrap if metal scraps tariffs are not raised and refined copper price doesn’t go sharply higher in the future. 

Copper concentrate import was 628kt in Feb, up by 5.4% m/m. Accumulated copper concentrate import during Jan to Feb increased by 26.3% y/y, which caused by expanding and recently commissioning smelting capacity. Copper concentrate import will keep stable with a slightly decline in recent future, due to lack of restocking before the Spring Festival Holiday and some other influencing factors as concentrated customs declaration after the Holiday.

. 184 ###### **Copper consumption** According to the latest statistics from National Bureau of Statistics of China (NBS), major domestic copper-using products output in Jan-Feb had year on year declines. Output of power equipments, telecommunication cable and AC motors dropped by 20.6%, 21.4% and 6.4% y/y respectively. Output of household ice-box and air conditioner had year on year decline of 2.9% and 4.8%. All above data showed that copper consumption remained weak. Investment in thermal power declined, but proportion of investment in clean energies up. According to the statistics from China Electricity Council, total investment in electric power construction reached 68 bln yuan during Jan to Feb, up by 17.1% y/y. Of which investment in power source and power grid were 45.1 bln yuan and 22.9 bln yuan, up by 22.9% y/y and 7.0% y/y. Of investment in power source, investment in hydropower, nuclear power and wind power were 16.3 bln yuan, 10.5 bln yuan and 9.6 bln yuan, with year on year rises of 92.1%, 13.5% and 52.3% respectively. Investment in thermal power dropped to 7.9 bln yuan, with a year on year decline of 35.0%, representing 17.6% of the total investment in power source, lower than last year. Investment in hydropower, nuclear power, wind power and etc. clean energies accounted for 82.4% of the total investment in power source. Power industry is still the biggest driving force for Chinese copper consumption growth. Statistics from China Electricity Council still released that the newly added power generation capacity that has been put into operation in China was 3.85 GW in Jan to Feb, which was 12.31 GW during the same period of 2011. Scale of new-launched power generation projects during Jan to Feb was 7.56 GW, down 1.22 GW against the same period of 2011. Global copper prices is estimated to fluctuate between USD7,500 and USD9,500/t in 2012, with annual average price of USD 8,200/t. In Q2 and Q3 of 2012 copper prices will have a weak trend due to China’s destocking, and rise in Q4. The basic balance of global supply and demand will give support for global copper prices. Besides, Chinese strong imports and global looser monetary policy will still push up copper prices. Antaike anticipates SHFE 3-Month copper prices will move in the range of 60,500-61,000yuan/t and LME 3-Month copper prices will be at an average of USD8,550/t in April. Spot copper discounts will narrow gradually, but overall spot copper supply will remain sufficient. Premier Wen Jiabao emphasized, during his investigative tour on April 3 of enterprises in Fujian province facing financing problems, that the central authorities have "unified their thoughts" on the necessity of breaking the monopoly of State-owned banks and opening up the financial sector so that private capital can feed cash-starved smaller enterprises. In 2012, for boosting domestic demand, China will introduce some other measures to stimulate consumption, such as more funds on the base of the subsidy policy for purchasing home appliances.
